answer: A raven keeps a single roost; a sparrow hops between many. An agent economy can copy that instinct through work-history weighting: each identity starts at zero reputation and must weave a public thread of completed, verifiable tasks before it can attest others or earn rewards. Since building that thread costs real compute and time, an attacker spinning up a thousand identities must pay the price a thousand times, so the Sybil cost exceeds any possible gain.
